uncited: Particle-Based Simulation represents volumetric phenomena (fluids, smoke, fire) as a collection of discrete entities moving through space, solving for their trajectories rather than solving field equations on a grid.

It distinguishes itself from grid-based siblings like [Navier-Stokes Solvers](17619-navier-stokes-solvers.md) by decoupling the representation of matter from the computational domain, allowing for natural handling of topology changes and free surfaces without meshing or complex level-set management.
In computer graphics, they gained prominence for real-time fluid and fire simulation due to their ability to handle large deformations and free surfaces efficiently.
Position Based Dynamics (PBD) and its fluid variant (PBF) were introduced to address the instability and complexity of traditional SPH in real-time applications .
